dedupe_keys.name: conus wide water availability and cost by source huc8 and county update 2026

description: This dataset maps how much new water is available, and at what cost, from five sources in over 2,500 watersheds of the contiguous United States: unappropriated surface water, unappropriated groundwater, appropriated water that could be transferred from its current use, recycled municipal wastewater and brackish groundwater. Availability accounts for institutional limits such as water rights, compacts, treaties and instream flows, set with the help of water managers, and costs cover acquiring, conveying and treating the water. Vincent Tidwell and Kyongho Son produced the 2026 update, which adds county resolution, at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, building on the 2014 western and 2018 eastern studies; the five datasets are available from the PNNL DataHub with an OSTI DOI, free to access, while raw data, scripts and GIS files are available from the authors on request. Coverage is national at HUC8 and county level. Licence: not stated for the resource; the describing article (doi:10; reuse terms therefore remain unverified.1088/1748-9326/9/6/064009) is CC-BY-3.0. Simulation uses: siting and costing new water supply for utilities and power plants in capacity planning, optimisation and drought adaptation. Related records: USGS public supply water use (data-usgs-public-supply-water-use-reanalysis-huc12) and AZ-Hydro (data-az-hydro-arizona-water-use-1896-2099).
